grammarName.en: Causative have/get something done · the passive

scenario: The office is being renovated over one chaotic week, and almost nothing is done by the team themselves — so the episode is built on the causative (have/get something done) and the passive. Kate: 'We're having the walls painted and the carpet cleaned this week.' Den: 'I finally got my chair fixed — it only took a year.' Pol: 'The kitchen is being redone, so the smoothie station has been moved.' Alex, delighted, 'I'm getting a nap pod installed... I wish.' Peter: 'Where do I sit? My desk was taken away yesterday.' Things go slightly wrong (the wrong colour gets used, the coffee machine gets unplugged), but it ends well: 'It all gets done in the end.' Warm, wry B2 humour. Use the causative clearly (have/get + object + past participle) and passives across tenses (is being painted, has been moved, was taken away, will be finished). Keep sentences B2 but crisp.
